messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The cracks are showing—even the loyalists are slipping, and the streets are humming with something new. Not just anger anymore, but the quiet kind of hope that comes when people start to believe the unthinkable might actually happen. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching too closely."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual sources are admitting they don’t know what’s coming next. The question isn’t *if* things are changing, but *how fast* and whether we’re ready when they do."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it if you listen close. The question isn’t if the wind’s coming, but whether we’ll be ready when it does."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now, even if they won’t say it out loud. The question isn’t *if* things break, but whether the pieces fall inward or outward, and how fast we’ll need to move when they do."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual signs are there, but the quiet ones: warehouses emptying, checks being ignored, even the shopkeepers dropping their guard. We’re not out of the woods yet, but the wind’s changing—just don’t ask me which way it’s blowing."*"
Sender 6: "*"The ship’s taking on water—no one’s at the helm, and the crew’s starting to whisper about jumping. Keep your head down, but if you hear from others, listen closely. The wind’s shifting, but we don’t know yet if it’s a storm or just the calm before."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual watchdogs have stopped barking. People are packing for a trip they haven’t booked yet, and the only thing moving smoothly is the silence. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a race, it’s a collapse waiting for a push."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now, even the ones who used to pretend not to. The question isn’t *if*, but *how* and *when*, and whether the guards will still be watching the door when the roof comes down."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual suspects are stepping back, and the streets are humming with something new. But we still don’t know if this is a collapse or a trap. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the exits."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. Even the quiet ones are asking questions they’d never dare voice before. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The walls have ears, and the wind could change fast."*"
Sender 11: "*"The cracks aren’t just showing—they’re spreading, and the regime knows it. My landlord, of all people, just asked if I had a way out. That’s not fear talking; that’s the math changing."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The usual rules don’t apply anymore, but we still need to move carefully. Let’s talk in person soon."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, and everyone’s quietly packing their bags. The cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if the roof will hold or come crashing down first. Stay sharp, and keep your plans loose."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking differently now, even the ones who used to whisper. The regime’s moves don’t add up, and the silence from the top is louder than any order. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but you can feel it. The usual watchers are watching each other now, and even the ones who always knew everything are admitting they don’t. Keep your heads down, but be ready—this isn’t just noise anymore."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who never spoke before are asking what comes next. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but how fast, and whether the guards will still be watching when it does."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint, the whole frame is shifting. The teachers’ slowdowns, the payments still coming in, the journalist’s pieces going unpunished—it’s not just us seeing it anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The air feels different, but we don’t know if it’s the storm breaking or the calm before the next lockdown."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls are shaking, and the guards don’t even seem to notice. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go fast, or it could be a test."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—just a little, but enough to let some light in. The old guard is fraying at the edges, the money men are hedging their bets, and even the censors seem to have dozed off for a second. But don’t mistake quiet for weak—they’re still sharpening their knives, and the streets aren’t ready to move yet. Stay sharp, stay small, and watch for the first real stumble."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and everyone’s just waiting to see which way it tilts. The usual signs are all there, but the real tell? Even the cautious ones are packing their bags quietly. We’re not just watching the storm anymore—we’re in it."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different now—not just the usual tension, but like something’s being tightened, not loosened. The pension checks came on time, the old songs play louder than ever, and the foreign press is packing their bags to come back. Not a storm yet, but the calm before one—let’s keep our ears open and our plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—even the merchants are packing up without a word, and the censors are too busy to keep up. But the pension checks still came on time, and the foreigners are betting on us lasting. So either the rot’s shallow, or the rot’s so deep no one’s noticed yet. Keep your ears open—especially for what the soldiers aren’t saying."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different now—not just frustration, but people quietly making moves. The usual cracks are showing, but the real question is whether the military’s silence is hesitation or a trap. Stay sharp, and keep your plans flexible."*"
Sender 24: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed. The usual checks and balances are slipping, and the people who used to keep things running smooth are suddenly quiet. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just another test. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for the storm, more like people are finally stepping out from under the eaves. The usual watchdogs seem distracted, and even the markets don’t flinch when we talk. But don’t mistake quiet for weakness—they’re still there, just deeper in the shadows. Let’s stay sharp, not reckless."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
